main_reason_for_recommendation: 14B feasibility directly tests Matt's stated goal of enabling 14B-class CPU inference. The approach is proven on 7B; whether it scales is the critical unknown. 14B canary provides high information gain with manageable risk, whereas backend integration is high-complexity with uncertain payoff.
main_risk: 14B model (~9GB) plus sidecars (~2.8GB INT8, ~2.7GB INT6) plus KV cache may approach or exceed the 15GB RAM ceiling — possible OOM failure
what_not_to_do_next: Continue CLI-level scalar loop optimization (diminishing returns confirmed)
Write public writeup without 14B validation (invites scale-limited criticism)
Attempt backend integration without design phase
Claim production readiness, universal speedup, or larger-than-7B support

phase16b_plan.title: Phase 16B: 14B Feasibility Canary
steps: Verify model SHA256 and update expected hash
Adapt sidecar generator for 14B tensor dimensions (M=24576, verify from model)
Tiny canary: n=8, c=128 — does it load without OOM and generate coherent output?
If canary passes: run 8-prompt × 80-token validation matrix (INT8, same as Phase 14P)
If canary OOMs: try INT6 instead (smaller sidecars)
Compare generation tok/s vs native 14B baseline
Record: loaded layers, unique SHA count, gen tok/s, quality assessment
Freeze with verdict: FEASIBLE_14B / PARTIAL_14B_FIT / INFEASIBLE_14B_HARDWARE

success_thresholds.FEASIBLE_14B: Loads without OOM, gen tok/s >= 5.0, quality degradations = 0
success_thresholds.PARTIAL_14B_FIT: Loads but gen tok/s < 5.0 — architecture works, hardware limit
success_thresholds.INFEASIBLE_14B_HARDWARE: OOM even with INT6 — need more RAM

hardware_assessment.verdict: Borderline — int6 likely fits, int8 is tight
